traits.leaf_area_per_basal_area.note: USDA Urban Tree Database (McPherson, van Doorn and Peper 2016, RDS-2016-0005), TS3 raw tree data: its 35 palo verdes (Parkinsonia aculeata and P. florida): 0.188 m² of leaf a cm². Median leaf area over trunk area at breast height of its open-grown street and park trees 20 cm or more through, the trees the broadleaf median (0.167) was taken over.

traits.crown_spread.note: USDA Urban Tree Database (McPherson, van Doorn and Peper 2016, RDS-2016-0005), TS3 raw tree data: its 18 palo verdes 25 years or older (Parkinsonia aculeata and P. florida): 1.21. Median crown width over height of its trees 25 years or older (15 or older where it has fewer than 10 that old), measured open-grown street and park trees.

traits.wood_density_basic_kg_m3.note: GWDD v.2.2 genus aggregate for Parkinsonia (gwddagg_v2.2_genus.csv, read): specific gravity 0.6 (wsg_est, the hierarchical-model genus mean, from 18 records in 11 sources); trunks 0.6, branches 0.58. A species with its own measurements states its own. Basic density is the specific gravity times 1000 kg/m3.

traits.note: Jepson eFlora's account of Parkinsonia, as search results quote it (the page itself was not read): flower bilateral; sepals more or less free and alike, generally reflexed; petals more or less equal, the banner widely ovate, generally cream-white, unlike the others (not a pea flower's); stamens 10, free, exserted; ovary generally one-chambered.
